pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Claves
   B. Cowbell
   C. Kayamba
   D. Xylophone

2. Which twigs are best for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Thick logs
   B. Wet, bent branches
   C. Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   D. Green leaves

3. What can be used as the core of an improvised macramé ball? (1 mark)
   A. A glass bottle
   B. A metal nail
   C. A large stone
   D. Crumpled paper or old cloth

4. Which attacker may NOT enter the goal circle? (1 mark)
   A. WA
   B. GA
   C. None
   D. GS

5. In an overhead pass, the ball starts (1 mark)
   A. above the head
   B. between the knees
   C. behind the knees
   D. at the ankles

6. What is the length of a full netball court? (1 mark)
   A. 50 metres
   B. 30.5 metres
   C. 100 metres
   D. 10 metres

7. Where can you get pictures for a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Old newspapers and magazines
   B. From a rock
   C. From the sky
   D. Only from the bank

8. How is flour paste made? (1 mark)
   A. Freeze flour
   B. Mix flour and sand
   C. Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   D. Burn flour

9. Which of these is a dark tone of red? (1 mark)
   A. Red mixed with yellow
   B. Red mixed with a little black
   C. Red mixed with white
   D. Red mixed with water

10. On the colour wheel, orange sits between (1 mark)
   A. yellow and blue
   B. blue and green
   C. red and blue
   D. red and yellow

11. Where do you place a soft shadow when painting a fruit on a table? (1 mark)
   A. On the table under the fruit
   B. Nowhere
   C. Inside the fruit
   D. On the ceiling

12. The steady pulse in a piece of music is called the (1 mark)
   A. lyric
   B. beat
   C. echo
   D. melody

13. Which is a way to give good feedback to a partner? (1 mark)
   A. Say nothing
   B. Push them
   C. Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   D. Laugh at their mistakes

14. In a crab balance, your tummy faces (1 mark)
   A. backwards
   B. sideways
   C. up
   D. down

15. Which muscles does the crab balance mainly strengthen? (1 mark)
   A. Only the ears
   B. Only the fingers
   C. Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   D. Only the eyes

16. In a side roll, you should keep your legs (1 mark)
   A. wide apart
   B. bent
   C. together with toes pointed
   D. lifted off the mat

17. In a crab balance, what is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Straight arms
   B. Hips sagging near the mat
   C. Head in line
   D. Hips lifted

18. Good manners for an audience include (1 mark)
   A. walking around
   B. throwing things
   C. talking loudly
   D. being quiet and clapping at the right time

19. When you give feedback on a friend's photograph you should (1 mark)
   A. say it is terrible
   B. say nothing
   C. say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   D. laugh

20. To keep the camera steady you should (1 mark)
   A. hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   B. shake it
   C. hold it at arm's length with one finger
   D. throw it

21. A blurred photograph is (1 mark)
   A. dark
   B. very clear
   C. always good
   D. not sharp

22. Why delete poor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. So memory is not filled up
   B. To make the screen dark
   C. To cool it
   D. To break the camera

23. A subject in photography is (1 mark)
   A. the battery
   B. the camera
   C. the person or thing you photograph
   D. the screen

24. On the staff, the note G sits on (1 mark)
   A. a space above the staff
   B. line 3
   C. the top line
   D. line 2

25. The top part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. head joint
   B. middle joint
   C. bell
   D. foot joint

26. A descant recorder is made of (1 mark)
   A. paper only
   B. glass
   C. plastic or wood
   D. metal foil only

27. Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should (1 mark)
   A. go in at night
   B. swim alone
   C. dive from rocks
   D. only go in with a trusted adult who can swim

28. What happens when the hawk tags the last chick? (1 mark)
   A. The game ends forever
   B. The hen goes home
   C. The hawk sleeps
   D. The chick becomes the hawk

29. Verse 1 of the anthem asks (1 mark)
   A. God to bless the nation
   B. for money
   C. for a holiday
   D. for a new school

30. Which is a component of a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. Price
   B. Weight
   C. Community of origin
   D. Distance

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give four ways to make a clear centre of interest. (4 marks)

32. Give four safety rules for animal games. (4 marks)

33. Where do the notes B, A and G sit on the staff? (3 marks)

34. What is a rest in music? (2 marks)

35. Explain the job of the drumhead and the shell of a drum. (3 marks)

36. State the jobs of the lens, the screen and the battery of a camera. (3 marks)

37. State three points of good sprinting technique. (3 marks)

38. When is an overhead pass better than a chest pass? (2 marks)

39. Explain how to compose a short melody using d, r and m. (4 marks)

40. Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet. (3 marks)

41. Name the three secondary colours and state how each is made. (3 marks)

42. State the recorder notes that match d, r and m. (3 marks)

43. Why is it important to appreciate the works of people from different cultures? (3 marks)

44. Describe how to make a chest pass. (4 marks)

45. Describe how partners should give feedback on each other's gymnastics. (3 marks)

46. What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Xylophone
   A xylophone has bars that give different notes, so it can play a tune.

2. C — Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   Dry, straight, thin twigs burn evenly into good drawing sticks.

3. D — Crumpled paper or old cloth
   Paper or cloth makes a soft core that keeps its shape.

4. A — WA
   The Wing Attack plays in the centre and goal thirds but not in the circle.

5. A — above the head
   The ball is lifted above the head before it is thrown.

6. B — 30.5 metres
   A full court is 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide.

7. A — Old newspapers and magazines
   Cut pictures from old papers and magazines.

8. C — Mix flour and cold water to a smooth paste, then add hot water while stirring
   An adult adds hot water to thicken the smooth paste.

9. B — Red mixed with a little black
   Adding black makes a darker shade of red.

10. D — red and yellow
   Orange is made from red and yellow, so it sits between them.

11. A — On the table under the fruit
   A shadow under the object makes it seem to sit on the table.

12. B — beat
   The beat is the steady pulse we tap or clap along to.

13. C — Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   Kind and helpful feedback includes praise and a suggestion.

14. C — up
   The tummy faces the ceiling like a table top.

15. C — Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   Holding the body up uses many muscle groups.

16. C — together with toes pointed
   Legs stay together to keep the log shape.

17. B — Hips sagging near the mat
   Hips should stay lifted to make the body level.

18. D — being quiet and clapping at the right time
   The audience should listen respectfully.

19. C — say what you like first and then suggest one improvement
   Kind and helpful feedback works best.

20. A — hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   A steady hold gives a sharp photograph.

21. D — not sharp
   Blurred means not sharp.

22. A — So memory is not filled up
   Deleting saves space.

23. C — the person or thing you photograph
   The subject is what you are photographing.

24. D — line 2
   G is on the second line from the bottom with the treble clef.

25. A — head joint
   The head joint has the mouthpiece.

26. C — plastic or wood
   Recorders are commonly made of plastic or wood.

27. D — only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   Open water is more dangerous.

28. D — The chick becomes the hawk
   Roles change so everyone plays.

29. A — God to bless the nation
   The first verse is a prayer for blessing.

30. C — Community of origin
   Components include community, type, message, participants and instruments.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the subject first; move closer; remove distractions; place the subject in the middle or slightly to the side; keep it sharp; bend to eye level. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Play on soft, clear ground; warm up; keep a distance from others; do not push or trip; drink water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: B is on line 3, A is in the space between line 2 and line 3, and G is on line 2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sign for silence for a certain length of time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for silence, 1 mark for length of time.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: The drumhead vibrates when struck and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drumhead, 2 marks for the shell's job explained.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: The lens lets light in; the screen shows the view and photos; the battery gives power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eyes look ahead; elbows bent and arms swing back and forth; knees lift high; land on the front of the foot; body leans forward slightly. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: When a defender stands close so that the ball must go over their arms.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a defender, 1 mark for going over.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give a syllable to each note. Use steps. End on d as a crotchet. Sing it and show the hand signs. Write the syllables under the rhythm names.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Orange from red and yellow, green from yellow and blue, purple from blue and red.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each secondary colour with its mixture.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: If G is doh, then G, A and B match d, r and m. G is d, A is r and B is m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: We learn about others, it builds respect and unity and it helps us value all cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold the ball at chest height with both hands. Look at the partner. Step forward and straighten the arms, turning the thumbs down. The ball goes to the partner's chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watch carefully, say one good thing first, then one thing to improve, and be kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.
